extracted.intended_audience: PCT applicants and International Searching/Preliminary/ Supplementary Examining Authorities (patent examiners)
extracted.subtask_short: PCT unity and prior art guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on assessing unity of invention, procedures for invitations to pay additional fees and protests at international search and preliminary examination stages, and rules for identifying and treating prior art and Internet disclosures under the PCT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (single general inventive concept) — Rule 13.1
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must relate to a single general inventive concept; groups of inventions must be so linked as to form a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether claims share the same or corresponding special technical feature(s) (see Rule 13.2). Analyze the technical features and the problems they solve; if special technical features solve different problems and do not correspond, unity is lacking. Example analyses: identify the special technical feature(s) of each claim and the technical problem(s) they solve to assess technical relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special technical feature correspondence — Rule 13.2
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions are considered unified only if they share one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the features of claims to see if they constitute corresponding special technical features. If features are so different that they do not share any same/corresponding special technical feature(s), the requirement of unity is not met (illustrated by examples such as steering-by-headgear vs hydraulic lifting mechanism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of separate inventions when unity lacking
rubrics_metrics.description: When lack of unity is found, the ISA/IPAE must identify the separate inventions or groups of inventions and indicate which claims belong to each invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group claims into distinct inventions (e.g., Invention 1: claim 1; Invention 2: claim 2). Explain common subject matter, whether common features are new/non-obvious, and specify the special technical features that make contributions over the prior art for each invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the invitation to pay additional fees — Form PCT/ISA/206
rubrics_metrics.description: After deciding lack of unity exists, the ISA informs the applicant by a communication containing an invitation to pay additional fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invitation must (i) specify the reasons for lack of unity (see paragraph 10.63), (ii) identify the separate inventions and indicate number/amount of additional search fees, and (iii) invite the applicant to pay, where applicable, the protest fee. The invitation precedes (but see exceptions) issuance of the international search report and written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and payment window for additional fees and protest fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional fees (and any protest fee) must be paid within one month from the date of the invitation for the ISA to search those inventions other than the first mentioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ISA cannot treat the application as withdrawn for lack of unity nor invite the applicant to amend claims; payment within the one-month time limit is required for further search. If applicant wishes to pay under protest, the additional fees (and protest fee if applicable) must be paid within the same one-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logically presented technical reasoning for lack of unity (required content)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invitation to pay additional fees must set out a logically presented, technical reasoning containing the basic considerations behind the finding of lack of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraph 10.63 and Rule 40.1. The reasoning should explain why the application is not considered to comply with the unity requirement and identify the special technical features and problems solved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search of additional inventions without payment of fees — practicality/economy exception (Rule 40.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If little or no additional search effort is required, the examiner may search one or more additional inventions while making the search for the main invention despite nonpayment of additional fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may occur when lack of unity is found a priori or a posteriori. Completion of the international search for those additional inventions will later require additional fees to be paid, and further classification units may need to be consulted when fees are paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing search/written opinion for additional inventions without requesting fees (exceptional circumstances)
rubrics_metrics.description: In exceptional cases where additional work is negligible, the examiner may complete the international search and written opinion for additional inventions together with the main invention without requesting additional fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should consider both search time and the time needed to prepare the written opinion, since written opinion work may justify requesting additional fees even if search effort is small. If total additional work does not justify requesting fees, include all results in the ISR but still state finding of lack of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest procedure at International Search Stage (Rule 40.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may protest an ISA’s allegation of lack of unity or that the number of additional fees is excessive and request a refund; protests are examined by an ISA review body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A protest must be a reasoned statement accompanying payment of the additional fee, explaining why requirements of unity are fulfilled and addressing reasons in the invitation. Additional search fees must be paid for any protest to be considered. An ISA may require payment of a protest fee. If the protest is found justified, fees (totally or partly) are refunded. Time limits and refund rules described in paragraphs 10.66–10.70 and 10.69.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial international search report option (ISA discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA may either immediately invite payment and search/continue to search the main invention or first carry out the search on the main invention and draw up a partial ISR to accompany the invitation to pay additional fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A partial ISR provides useful information to the applicant to decide whether to pay additional search fees. The examiner should endeavor to ensure searches are made early to enable compliance with Rule 42 time limits (paragraph 10.62).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Preliminary Examination — handling lack of unity (Article 34(3), Rule 68)
rubrics_metrics.description: During international preliminary examination, if examiner finds lack of unity, a communication may be sent inviting applicant within one month to restrict claims or to pay an additional fee for each additional invention; at least one possible restriction should be indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invitation (Form PCT/IPEA/405) must set out a logically presented technical reasoning per Guidelines. If the applicant does not comply, the international preliminary examination report is established on the parts relating to the main invention (first mentioned in claims if in doubt). Alternatively, when little/no additional effort is involved, the examiner may carry out preliminary examination for the entire application and indicate lack of unity in the report (paragraphs 10.74–10.76).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest procedure at International Preliminary Examination Stage (Rule 68.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may protest lack of unity in IPEA invitation or that required additional fees are excessive and request refund; protests are examined by a review body within the IPEA framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protest is a reasoned statement accompanying payment of the additional fee; additional examination fees must be paid for protest to be considered. IPEA may require a protest fee; refund rules and time limits mirror those at the search stage (paragraphs 10.78–10.82). Texts of protest and decision may be notified to elected Offices on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary international search: no additional-fee option (Rule 45bis.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the supplementary international search stage there is no opportunity to pay additional fees for further inventions; the supplementary international search report should be established immediately on the main invention only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Authority specified for supplementary search may assess unity but should take into account the opinion of the main ISA and any protest/decision received before the supplementary search starts. If examiner finds lack of unity, explain in Box No. III of the supplementary ISR; if differing from main ISA, set out full reasoning for applicant and third parties (paragraphs 10.83–10.85).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of the main invention for search stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The main invention will normally be the invention first mentioned in the claims, but the examiner should exercise discretion where the first-mentioned invention is not searchable or the applicant requests a different selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include when the first-mentioned invention is unclear, excluded from search, or has been shown to be completely anticipated by the main international search; applicant requests to limit supplementary search to an invention other than the first mentioned should be respected (paragraph 10.86).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of opinion for supplementary international search (request and consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request review of the examiner’s opinion on unity of invention within one month of supplementary ISR notification; request may be subject to a review fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If opinion is found at least partly unjustified, issue revised supplementary ISR stating revised view and include search results for claims that should have been included. If opinion entirely unjustified, refund review fee (paragraphs 10.87–10.88).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of prior art (Article 33(2); Rule 33.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art is defined as 'everything made available to the public anywhere in the world by any means' before the relevant date for assessing novelty and inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no restrictions as to geography, language, manner (including Internet disclosures) or age of prior art. Admissions by the applicant (e.g., label 'prior art') may constitute prior art but can be rebutted. Distinguish different definitions of 'relevant date' for ISR vs written opinion/IPER (see paragraphs 11.02–11.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant date for international search report purposes (Rule 33.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ISR purposes 'relevant date' is the international filing date of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potentially relevant disclosures should be included in the ISR if made available to the public prior to the international filing date to ensure completeness even if national authorities disagree with priority claims (paragraph 11.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant date for written opinion and international preliminary examination (Rule 64.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For written opinion and IPER purposes the relevant date is generally the international filing date, except where a valid earlier priority date applies (see Rule 64.1 and paragraph 11.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where priority is claimed and within the priority period, the filing date of the earlier application may be the relevant date unless the priority claim is invalid. Examiner must consider documents published between claimed priority date and international filing date and may base written opinion on claimed priority date if insufficient time to determine priority validity (see paragraphs 6.17 and 17.29(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents casting doubt on priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents showing that a priority claim might not be justified should be mentioned in the ISR and explained in the written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No special search is normally made to determine priority validity unless a special reason exists (e.g., continuation-in-part, differing country of residence), but such documents should be reported and, if relevant, may justify some extension of the search (paragraph 11.06).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of later-published but earlier-filed patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For ISR purposes, published patent applications or patents whose filing (or claimed priority) date is earlier than the international filing date must be included even if their publication date is the same as or later than the ISR date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international preliminary examination these earlier-filed but later-published applications are not part of the prior art for novelty/inventive step but must be drawn to attention in the written opinion/IPER per Rule 70.10 with publication/filing/priority dates and any opinion on invalid priority claims (paragraphs 11.07–11.09).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copending applications and double patenting issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-pending international applications of the same date may raise double-patenting issues; if from the same applicant and relating to the same invention, cite as 'L' in the ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner is aware that applicant has a national application with same priority date and same invention, a notification to the applicant alone is given. No notification where two different applicants have concurrent filings (paragraph 11.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing later documents relevant to understanding the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents published on or after the international filing date may still be relevant for understanding the invention (e.g., theory underlying invention or showing incorrect reasoning) and may be cited in the ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The international search is not extended for this purpose, but such documents known to the examiner may be selected for citation in the ISR and their relevance explained in the written opinion (paragraph 11.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of disclosure — availability to the public (general test)
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclosure is regarded as made available to the public if, at the relevant date, members of the public could gain knowledge of the content and there was no bar of confidentiality restricting use or dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of an index/catalogue does not automatically make content inaccessible — apply the accessibility principle. Where only month/year given, presume availability on the last day of that month/year unless evidence shows otherwise (paragraph 11.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet disclosures treated as prior art (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet/on-line database disclosures are considered in the same manner as other forms of disclosure; they are publicly available as of the date the disclosure was publicly posted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problems can arise establishing publication date and whether the content was modified. Distinguish disclosures on trusted publishers' web sites (on-line journals, newspapers — take publication date at face value unless evidence to contrary) from web sites of unknown reliability (use technical means to attempt to establish publication date). Authorities may need to query website owners to establish date where only month/year is given (paragraphs 11.13–11.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling Internet disclosures from web sites of unknown reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an Internet disclosure comes from a site of unknown reliability and gives no explicit publication date, the Authority may use technical means available to attempt to reveal the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical means (enumerated in following paragraphs) may be used to establish date. Examiner should attempt to establish publication date and reliability before relying on the Internet disclosure as prior art (paragraph 11.16–11.17).
